Senses.Explanation: A person's capacity to speak is what Chan verdicts test, trust, disable, or demand under the image of the tongue. Yungai Jipeng and Chengtian Weijian each answer a public question by saying that the tongue has no bone. Guanghui Yuanlian says that he no longer doubts the tongues of old masters, and Shoushan Xingnian immediately asks him to state his understanding. Huangbo Xiyun predicts that Linji Yixuan will cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven. Longyuan Fa says that a demon king has cut off the Buddha's tongue and offers to redress the wrong. Huiyun Benchong Sheng orders a respondent to produce a statement without moving the tongue, then says the respondent's shout still involves lips and mouth. These are speech acts and verdicts, not reports of bodily injury, so they establish a Zen-loaded referent separate from the organ that can be bitten.
Senses.Note: The headword has 2,473 hits in 325 allowlisted texts. Six speech-capacity anchors plus two bodily anchors meet the eight-occurrence floor. The two PreferredTargets name distinguishable referents: an ability to speak and a body part.

Occurrences.Kwic: 住後僧問。如何是佛法大意。師曰。舌頭無骨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), section on Yungai Jipeng: asked the great meaning of the buddha teaching, Yungai answers that the tongue has no bone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問開口即失閉口即喪。未審如何說。師曰。舌頭無骨。僧曰。不會。師曰。對牛彈琴。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), section on Chengtian Weijian: Chengtian answers the open-mouth/closed-mouth dilemma by saying the tongue has no bone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師當下大悟云。某甲不疑天下老和尚舌頭也。山曰。汝會處作麼生。與我說來看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), section on Guanghui Yuanlian: Yuanlian says he no longer doubts old masters' tongues, and Shoushan Xingnian asks him to state what he understands.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), succession account of Linji Yixuan: Huangbo Xiyun predicts that Linji will cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collected Raising of Old Cases of the School (宗門拈古彙集): commentator Longyuan Fa says that a demon king has cut off the Buddha's tongue and that Longyuan will redress the wrong.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，僧出擬問，師曰：不動舌頭道將一句來。僧喝，師曰：猶涉唇吻在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Lamp Collection, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Huiyun Benchong Sheng: Huiyun demands a statement without moving the tongue and says the respondent's shout still involves lips and mouth.

Senses.Explanation: The tongue is also the bodily organ that can be bitten and injured. Wanru Tongwei speaks of biting the tongue while eating, and Jingting Zong speaks of biting through it while eating melon seeds. These physical predicates require anatomy rather than speaking capacity.
Senses.Note: Two independent bodily witnesses establish the ordinary anatomical referent. No special Zen deviation is asserted for it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In his Recorded Sayings (萬如禪師語錄), Wanru Tongwei speaks of biting the tongue while eating.
In his Recorded Sayings (逕庭宗禪師語錄), Jingting Zong says that just then he bit through his tongue while eating melon seeds.
